sections.body:
This is a story about Tuấn. He is ten years old and he is a small explorer. His explorer name is Captain Bảy.

His grandmother has just moved to a house by the sea. Everything of hers is in boxes now, and one rainy afternoon Tuấn helps to open them.

In the last box there is a wooden box with no lock. Inside it there is a folded piece of paper. It is a **map**. A map is a drawing of a place, seen from above.

The map is old. The paper is soft and the ink has gone brown. At the top it says: For the captain. Three clues. One treasure. Do not dig where the birds sit.

A good adventure has a shape. It has a beginning, a middle and an end. The beginning tells you who is going and why. The middle brings the surprise. The end gives you something worth keeping.

Read it slowly. Then tell it to someone else. That is how an adventure becomes yours.
examples: This story is about a boy who looks for hidden treasure.
A map is a drawing of a place, seen from above.
I can tell this story again tomorrow.
sections.heading: What this treasure hunt is about

sections.body:
Tuấn reads the map at the kitchen table. He reads it twice.

The first **clue** is written in rhyme: "Where the hill drinks the morning, look beneath the seat of the hill." A clue is a small hint. It does not tell you everything. It tells you where to look next.

His grandmother watches him over her cup of tea. She says nothing. Her eyes are smiling.

The second clue is a picture: a round thing with a needle in it. A **compass**. A compass is a small tool with a needle that points north. Explorers carry one so they never walk in circles.

Tuấn has a compass. It is yellow plastic and the needle is a bit shaky. But it is enough.

The third clue is a picture of a bench, and under the bench a small nail.

The afternoon is long and warm. Tuấn puts the map in his pocket, says goodbye to his grandmother, and goes up the hill.
examples: The first clue was written in rhyme.
The third clue was a picture of a bench and a nail.
sections.heading: How the hunt began

sections.body:
On the hill there is a **hill** of grass, an old bench, and a lot of ants.

The first thing Tuấn does is the wrong thing. He digs in the first soft place he sees. He digs for ten minutes, and his hands get brown. There is nothing there but a bottle cap and a worried worm.

Then he reads the rhyme again. "Where the hill drinks the morning." He looks up. At the top of the hill there is a stone bowl where the rain water sits in the morning. The morning water comes down from there.

So he follows the water. The compass helps him walk in a straight line. Halfway down, the needle spins, because Tuấn is standing on a big piece of iron in the ground. He laughs and writes that on the map: compass goes crazy here.

At the bottom of the water line he finds the bench. It is old and green and covered in moss.

Under the bench there is a small iron nail. And beside the nail, the earth is a little bit different. It is softer, and it has a square edge.

Tuấn digs again, and this time he digs carefully. Slowly. The soil comes up in small squares, like little blocks.
examples: He dug in the wrong place and found a bottle cap.
The compass needle spun because of the iron in the ground.
The earth beside the nail was soft and square.
sections.heading: The middle: three clues and a hungry hill

sections.body:
The box is not gold.

It is a wooden box, the size of a shoebox, and it is full of paper. Old letters, tied with string. Photographs in a thin plastic sheet. A school report card with a very good mark in it. A pressed flower that is now brown.

At the bottom there is one more thing: a small tin of biscuits, and a note.

The note is in his grandmother's handwriting. It says: For Captain Bảy. I hid the good treasure so you would have to look for it. The gold is in the attic, in the tin with the buttons. I wanted you to find the rest.

Tuấn sits on the grass with the letters in his lap and reads them all. His grandmother wrote about a stormy day in 1985. About a bicycle with a loose wheel. About how small he was when he first ran to the sea.

She did not forget one single thing.

Then Tuấn walks home with the box on his shoulder. It is heavy, but not heavy from gold.

The real treasure was never in the ground. It was in the fact that somebody loved him enough to hide a story where he would find it.
examples: The box was full of letters and photographs.
She wanted him to find the story, not the gold.
The real treasure was never in the ground.
sections.heading: The surprise: what was inside the box

sections.body:
These are the words you will meet in this story. Learn them here, and you can use them in your own sentences.

A **treasure** is something you want very much and keep safe. It can be gold, but it can also be a letter or a photograph.

A **map** is a drawing of a place, seen from above. A map shows you the way, and it shows you where things are.

A **clue** is a small hint. Clues come one after another, and each one points to the next.

A **compass** is a small tool with a needle that points north. Explorers use a compass so they walk in a straight line.

A **hill** is a small mountain, high in the middle and low at the edges. You can walk up a hill in a few minutes if you are not tired.
examples: A treasure can be a letter, not only gold.
A map shows you the way from above.
sections.heading: The words inside this story

terms.example: The box in the grass held the real treasure.
terms.gloss: Something you want very much and keep safe. It can be gold, but it can also be a letter or a photograph.

terms.example: Tuấn unfolded the old map on the kitchen table.
terms.gloss: A drawing of a place, seen from above. A map shows you the way and shows you where things are.

terms.example: The third clue was a picture of a bench and a nail.

terms.gloss: A small tool with a needle that points north. Explorers use a compass so they walk in a straight line.

sections.body:
What did Tuấn learn? He learned that a good clue does not shout. It waits until you are ready to look.

He also learned that digging in the wrong place is not a failure. It is how he learned where the right place was.

Here is how to tell this adventure to someone. Keep the order, and the surprise will land in the right place.

Start with the map in the attic. Tell the three clues in the middle, including the hole in the wrong place. Save the box of letters for last. Then say the small lesson in one short sentence.

The lesson of this adventure is this: some treasures are too heavy for a shovel.
examples: The story starts with a map in an attic.
The surprise comes at the very end.
Some treasures are too heavy for a shovel.
sections.heading: The small lesson, and how to tell the story
steps: Start with the character: Tuấn opening the last box in the attic.
Tell the middle: the rhyme, the compass, the bench and the wrong hole.
Tell the surprise: the box of letters and the note from his grandmother.
End with the lesson: some treasures are too heavy for a shovel.

item.summary: Tuấn finds an old map in his grandmother's attic and walks across the hill to look for buried treasure. Follow him through three clues, a compass with a shaky needle and a long afternoon of digging. After reading, you can retell the hunt, use five new explorer words in your own sentences, and say what the real treasure was.
item.title: The Little Explorer and the Hidden Treasure
